analysis.title: GS Basics Land & Power. 2027 vs 2029. Vol Compression
key_insights: Equity futures dipped sharply overnight after the election results, then recovered. Rich Privorotsky (GS) suspects vol will struggle to sustain a bid and that the initial selloff gets absorbed as investors pick apart what they want to own.
Multiples have been de-rated aggressively, particularly across AI infrastructure. Hedges put on over the past few days now need to be monetized.

The AI debate is shifting from the cost of compute to whether capacity can be permitted, energized and delivered in 2027/28/29. Moratoriums, local opposition to data centers and tighter regulation could constrain supply.

If supply is constrained, customers of chip, cooling and electrical equipment vendors may have overordered relative to capacity they can energize. This is potentially negative for picks and shovels, though GS says much of that risk appears reflected in multiples.

Scarce energized compute could gain scarcity value, which potentially benefits hyperscalers and owners of deployed capacity. Throttling supply may push pricing higher for longer rather than destroy demand.
Neoclouds are not all the same. Some have substantial existing compute and contracted demand, while others depend on new facilities, financing and power delivery.

On policy horizons, uncertainty over corporate tax rates, antitrust/M&A and oversight in 2029 can cap terminal multiples. GS argues that with current administration leadership through 2028, corporate decision makers have an incentive to pull forward capital deployment, permitting and transactions into 2027.
The S&P 500 has been higher 12 months after all 19 midterm election cycles since 1950.
AMD reported revenue +45% YoY to $13.4bn and data center +97% to $8.5bn, with Q4 guidance implying another 27% sequential acceleration. GS calls it the micro evidence the AI trade needed.
Intel's data center business grew 78% YoY, so GS reads Intel as a supply/execution and profitability story, not a demand warning.
GS finds it hard to reconcile AMD's accelerating growth with the scale of multiple compression across the AI complex.

Geopolitics is the swing factor. Mediators are still exchanging proposals, a limited deal is possible but the sides remain far apart, and trilateral Russia/Ukraine/US talks are scheduled in Abu Dhabi on November 10-11.
GS's view: AI infrastructure has been sold to death, positioning looks considerably cleaner, and vol likely comes in quickly, which drives spot in the short term.

GS calls Intel a poor read-through for the AI complex but a supply/execution and profitability story. Data center grew 78% YoY, so demand was not the problem.

risk_factors: Geopolitics could move markets either way very quickly.
Permitting, moratoriums, local opposition to data centers and a more restrictive regulatory environment could constrain compute supply.
Customers of data center suppliers may have overordered relative to capacity they can energize.
Neoclouds dependent on new facilities, financing and power delivery carry more risk.
Uncertainty over future corporate tax rates, antitrust/M&A and administrative oversight could cap terminal multiples.
vol_and_positioning: GS expects vol to struggle to sustain a bid, with many hedges placed over recent days that now need to be monetized.
GS says positioning looks considerably cleaner and that vol likely comes in quickly, driving spot in the short term.
Side-note in the report: VXN vol quite elevated (Bloomberg, as of 4/11/2026).
geopolitical: Mediators are still exchanging proposals to bridge differences. A limited deal is possible, but the two sides remain far apart. The outcome could be escalation or continued negotiations.
Trilateral Russia/Ukraine/US talks are scheduled in Abu Dhabi on November 10-11.
Texas governor race: Gina Hinojosa defeated Abbott (AP).
